2607.27487.title: INCLAIR: Inception-Based Longitudinal Clinical Anomaly Detection with Informed Reasoning
2607.27487.paper_summary: Detecting anomalies in longitudinal clinical profiles is clinically important but difficult: abnormal evidence is often sparse, patient histories have unequal length, and expert explanations are costly. We propose INCLAIR, a framework that scores each observation against multiple historical contexts, aggregates evidence at the profile level, and generates grounded natural-language explanations under limited expert supervision. Under stated within-profile exchangeability assumptions, the complete mean subsequence score takes an order-$l$ U-statistic form, yielding a variance decomposition and an incomplete-subset approximation that controls combinatorial inference cost independently of profile length. The same analysis shows that mean aggregation attenuates localized anomalies by a factor set by the anomaly support and profile length, motivating validation-selected top-$k$ pooling. Across three clinical datasets, INCLAIR consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines. We further validate practical relevance through a case study on longitudinal steroid profiles, comparing INCLAIR's predictions and explanations against domain-expert assessments supported by DNA analysis. The results show that INCLAIR enables clinically actionable anomaly detection under limited expert supervision.
2607.27487.paper_summary_zh: 檢測縱向臨床資料中的異常對臨床來說非常重要但也很困難：異常證據通常稀少，病歷長度不均，且專家解釋的成本高昂。 我們提出了INCLAIR，一個對每個觀察結果根據多個歷史背景進行評分的框架，並在資料層面上聚合證據，生成在有限專家監督下的有根據的自然語言解釋。 在所述的資料內部可交換性假設下，完整的均值子序列分數採用順序-$l$ U-統計量形式，產生方差分解和不完整子集近似，獨立於資料長度控制組合推斷成本。 相同的分析顯示，均值聚合通過由異常支持和資料長度設定的因子來減弱局部異常，這促使了經驗驗證選擇的前$k$池化。 在三個臨床數據集中，INCLAIR始終超越最先進的基準。 我們進一步通過對縱向類固醇資料的案例研究來驗證實際相關性，將INCLAIR的預測和解釋與由DNA分析支持的領域專家評估進行比較。 結果顯示，INCLAIR在有限的專家監督下實現了臨床可操作的異常檢測。
